summary: AI observability has become critical as LLM deployments scale, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams fly blind on latency spikes, prompt regressions, runaway token costs, and model quality degradation across production pipelines. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028, up from just 15% in early 2026, reflecting how central these tools have become to responsible AI operations.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain executions, agent runs, prompt versions, evaluation scores, and dataset-driven test results across LangChain and non-LangChain workflows
features: End-to-end trace capture with span-level detail
Prompt versioning and A/B comparison
Built-in evaluation datasets and human annotation queues
Regression testing against golden datasets
Integration with LangChain, LangGraph, and custom SDKs
Team collaboration with project-level access controls
Online and offline evaluation support
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage around $2.50 per thousand traces at standard retention; Enterprise pricing available
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need deep prompt versioning, evaluation pipelines, and collaborative debugging in a managed cloud environment

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, cost per call, latency, error rates, and user-level usage patterns via a proxy gateway layer
features: One-line proxy setup with minimal code changes
Real-time cost tracking and budget alerts by user, model, or endpoint
Request caching to reduce redundant API spend
Rate limiting and access control per API key
Prompt templating and versioning
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Open-source and self-hostable
Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, and other providers
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month with unlimited seats and usage-based overages; Team at $799/month adding SOC-2 and HIPAA; custom Enterprise with SAML SSO and on-prem options. Managed cloud approximately £20/month for 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing cost visibility and fast setup who want the simplest path to tracking spend across multiple LLM providers without heavy instrumentation

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiment runs, model evaluation metrics, dataset versions, prompt iterations, and multi-step agent workflows
features: Weave tracing for LLM calls and agent chains
Experiment tracking with rich artifact versioning
Built-in evaluation framework with custom scorers
Dataset management and lineage tracking
Collaborative dashboards for comparing runs
Integrations with major LLM frameworks and providers
Strong support for fine-tuning and training observability alongside inference
Model registry for production deployment tracking
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50/seat/month; Enterprise pricing on request. Core ML experiment tracking has been free for open-source projects.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams who need to unify training experiment tracking, fine-tuning workflows, and LLM inference observability in a single platform without switching tools

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM span-level traces, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, embedding drift, latency, error rates, hallucination signals, and enterprise-scale telemetry
features: Span-level distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry support
Dashboards for latency, error rates, and token throughput
Experiment-style workflows for comparing prompt or model runs
RAG pipeline evaluation including context relevance and faithfulness
Embedding drift and data quality monitoring
Online evaluations with LLM-as-judge and custom evaluators
Phoenix open-source version for local and self-hosted use
Enterprise telemetry with alerting and SLA monitoring
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AI managed platform offers a free developer tier, with Growth and Enterprise plans priced based on volume and features — contact sales for enterprise quotes
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing robust RAG evaluation, embedding monitoring, and production-grade telemetry that connects LLM performance to broader ML infrastructure

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, evaluation scores, session-level user interactions, token usage, latency, and custom application metrics
features: Detailed LLM tracing with nested spans and metadata
Prompt management with versioning and rollback
Custom score hooks for human and automated evaluations
Session and user-level analytics
Dataset creation from production traces for offline evaluation
Self-hosting option for full data control under MIT license
Strong community adoption and active open-source development
Integrations with OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and more
tools.pricing: Langfuse Cloud free for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud tiers start at approximately £20/month for higher volumes; self-hosted is free with infrastructure costs estimated around £30/month plus approximately 2 hours of maintenance per month
tools.best_for: Teams wanting open-source traceability with full data sovereignty, especially those with compliance requirements who prefer self-hosting over managed cloud solutions

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token counts, latency, and model metadata through OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation across any supported LLM provider or framework
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK requiring minimal code changes
Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and major LLM frameworks
Vendor-agnostic — sends data to any OTel-compatible backend (Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, etc.)
Trace and span capture compatible with existing observability stacks
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
Lightweight integration without proprietary lock-in
Supports Python and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs depend entirely on the backend observability platform you route telemetry to (e.g., Datadog, Grafana Cloud, or self-hosted Jaeger)
tools.best_for: Engineering teams with an existing OpenTelemetry-based observability stack who want to add LLM-specific instrumentation without adopting a new proprietary platform

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM response quality through 50+ evaluation metrics covering hallucination, answer relevancy, faithfulness, toxicity, bias, and contextual precision in RAG and agentic workflows
features: 50+ open-source evaluation metrics via DeepEval library
LLM-as-judge evaluations with customizable thresholds
RAG pipeline metrics including context recall and faithfulness
Regression testing against evaluation datasets
Online production evaluations integrated into the observability layer
CI/CD pipeline integration for automated quality gates
Used by teams at OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft
Dashboard for tracking metric trends over time
tools.pricing: DeepEval is open-source and free; Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier with paid plans for higher evaluation volumes and team collaboration features — see website for current pricing
tools.best_for: Teams who prioritize evaluation depth and want automated, metric-driven quality gates for RAG systems and agentic pipelines as part of their CI/CD and production monitoring workflow

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, costs, and completions unified alongside full infrastructure monitoring including logs, metrics, distributed traces, and frontend Real User Monitoring (RUM)
features: Unified platform for LLM observability and DevOps telemetry in a single deployment
Prompt tracing with input/output capture and latency tracking
Cost tracking per model, user, and endpoint
Infrastructure logs, metrics, and traces eliminating need for separate stacks
Frontend RUM monitoring included
Open-source and self-hostable
Significantly lower storage costs compared to Elasticsearch-based stacks
Compatible with OpenTelemetry collectors
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host; Helicone Cloud managed offering available with consumption-based pricing — see website for current tiers
tools.best_for: Platform and DevOps teams who want to consolidate LLM observability with infrastructure monitoring into one tool, avoiding the overhead of running separate dedicated stacks

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: Tools like Helicone offer built-in caching so identical or near-identical prompts return stored responses without hitting the LLM API, which can cut redundant spend by 20-40% for high-repetition use cases like FAQ bots or templated workflows.

Right-size your model selection per task: Use smaller, cheaper models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku, or Gemini Flash) for simple classification, summarization, or routing tasks, reserving frontier models only for complex reasoning. Observability tools with per-request cost tracking make it straightforward to identify which tasks are over-engineered and could be downgraded.

Set token budgets, rate limits, and cost alerts at the user and endpoint level: Platforms like Helicone and LangSmith allow you to cap spending per API key or user session, preventing runaway costs from loops, retries, or abuse before they appear on your monthly bill.

Continuously evaluate and shorten prompts using tracing data: LLM observability tools capture full prompt and completion text, making it easy to audit verbose system prompts or chain steps that add tokens without improving output quality. Regularly reviewing traces to trim unnecessary context, remove redundant instructions, and tighten few-shot examples can reduce average token counts by 15-30% without degrading response quality.
